questions.question: Where the trailing figures on a follower row are computed, every call site of format_watch_transition and _fleet_counts, and which of them pass a session.
questions.answer: The trailing figures on a row are counted by _fleet_counts in reckon/crew/recovery.py and turned into the dust-capped cells by the ticker's _stats; neither the render surface nor the CLI counts them. Every production call site of _fleet_counts except one passes no session, so a follower's trailing figures are the fleet's totals unless the event is re-scoped first. The only re-scoping call site is _fleet_counts(current, session=session) inside _scoped_watch_event (recovery.py:4025), which format_watch_transition reaches only when it is itself given a session (recovery.py:4061). The CLI's follow path does NOT give it one: the session there goes only to _follow_render_event, which blanks the owner column and leaves the figures alone. The one path that narrows the population is therefore reachable from the API but unused by the command a coordinator actually runs.

computation_sites.note: Counts the working/blocked/unpromoted partitions over live-pointer snapshots. The session keyword narrows the counted population; the docstring at line 3663 reads 'session narrows the counted population to the runs that session owns'.

questions.question: Where the follower de-duplicates a run's state, so a blocked or unpromoted run is printed once, and which existing hook a periodic line could use without breaking the rule that the stream carries only transitions and posture. on_poll in _follow_watch_lines is the candidate to confirm or reject.
questions.answer: The de-duplication is the reported map in _follow_watch_lines, keyed by run_id and holding the last state emitted for that run: _emit returns None when the incoming state equals the remembered one, so a run that stays blocked or unpromoted is printed once. on_poll is REJECTED as the vehicle for a periodic line, on a mechanical fact rather than a preference: _tick calls on_poll and discards its return value, and the caller's own poll callback returns None, so anything on_poll does has no channel back to the generator that yields to the pane. The correct site is inside the generator's own wait pass, where _tick() is already called (cli.py:1881 and 1905), because that code is in the generator and can yield. A periodic fleet-posture line emitted there would not break the transitions-and-posture rule: the fleet posture is exactly what the baseline already carries, and the comment at line 1862 restrains the follower's own facts from the stream, not the fleet's posture.

hook_verdict.why: _tick() calls on_poll and returns None, and the registered callback poll() also returns None; there is no yield channel from on_poll to the pane.

rule_scope.note: The full comment (1859-1862) says nothing about the follower itself goes on this stream, a reader wanting worker transitions and the fleet posture. A periodic fleet-posture line is posture, not the follower's own fact, so the rule does not forbid it; it only requires the line to be yielded from the generator, which rules out on_poll.

positive_control.note: The baseline is the existing precedent for posture on the stream, so a periodic line is a second emission of the kind already present rather than a new kind.

questions.question: Whether the recovery sweep a follower runs acts on runs of sessions other than the follower's own. Trace _sweep_lapsed_holds into reckon/crew/resumption.py and any review dispatch it reaches. Check the record of run r-20260922T161442206389 and state which session and process launched it.
questions.answer: YES. The sweep acts on the whole project, not the follower's session. _sweep_lapsed_holds is a delegator to resumption.sweep(project, dry_run=...), and sweep iterates list_live(project=project) with no session argument, then runs an automatic review pass whose own comment fixes it to the same site as the resume pass. A follower runs the sweep on a cadence, so any follower's sweep reaches every session's runs in the project and may dispatch a review onto a peer's scoring run. The named run's own record confirms it: r-20260922T161442206389 is a review of nova's run r-20260922T153201482175-sgc-sweep-control-at-the-four-of-twenty-revision, dispatched from the runtime session 576a27e3 while the run itself was recorded under crew session s18-fable-20260922.

questions.question: Where attach_line is composed, what executable it names, every surface that prints it to a coordinator, and whether it resolves from a shell whose PATH lacks the reckon virtual environment.
questions.answer: attach_line is composed by _watch_attach_line in reckon/crew/runs.py, which builds a parts list whose first element is the bare word reckon and appends the project and an optional --session. It names the executable reckon with no path; the docstring says this is one bare command on purpose, because a shell pipeline around it has three ways to swallow the ticker silently. Nine surfaces print or carry it. The emitted command does NOT resolve from a shell whose PATH lacks the reckon virtual environment: an invocation exits 127 with 'reckon: command not found'. Probe receipt: with the venv bin on PATH, command -v reckon prints /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/reckon; with a PATH of /usr/bin:/bin it is absent.

docstring_quote.quote: It is one bare command on purpose: filtering and buffering belong inside
